seoTitle: How to Cancel a TurboTax Return: Step-by-Step Guide
metaDescription: TurboTax has no literal cancel button. Here's how Clear & Start Over works, exactly what disables it, and what to do once it's no longer an option.
intro: Made a mistake early in a TurboTax return and want a clean slate? TurboTax doesn't have a button labeled "Cancel return." What it offers instead is Clear & Start Over, which erases your entered tax data so you can begin again, and it only works up to a specific point. This guide shows where that option lives, exactly what disables it, and what your real alternative is once it's gone.
prerequisites: A TurboTax Online return you haven't yet paid for, registered, or had a fee deducted from your refund. Clear & Start Over stops being available once any of those has happened, even if you technically haven't filed.

steps.heading: Sign in to your TurboTax account
steps.body: Go to TurboTax and sign in with the phone number, email, or user ID tied to your return. The sign-in page sits alongside TurboTax's marketing content about expert help and tax breaks, so look for the "Let's get you in to TurboTax" card on the right side of the page. If you've used TurboTax before, your email is often pre-filled and you just need your password.

image.caption: TurboTax's sign-in card, where you enter your account email or user ID to reach an in-progress return.

steps.heading: Open Tax home and locate your in-progress return
steps.body: After signing in, you land on Tax home, greeted by name with a summary of where your return stands. A checklist down the left side covers My info, Federal, State, Final review, and File, with green checkmarks next to whatever sections are already complete. The main panel shows an "Up next" card with a Continue filing button and the date you last saved. Glance at this checklist before clearing anything, so you understand how much progress you'd be giving up.

image.caption: The Tax home screen, showing a completed checklist for My info, Federal, State, and Final review, with Continue filing as the next step.

steps.heading: Find Clear & Start Over under Tax tools
steps.body: The option isn't on the main Tax home screen. TurboTax's own support instructions place it under Tax Tools in the left sidebar, then inside a Tools submenu (not as a sibling item next to Tools, the way it can look at a glance), alongside Print Center. TurboTax also notes you can reach the same starting point from Switch Products in the left menu. Opening it doesn't wipe anything immediately. It walks you to a confirmation screen titled "Are you sure you want to clear and start fresh?" which gives you one last chance to back out.

steps.heading: Read the warning before you confirm
steps.body: TurboTax spells out exactly what clearing does: you'll be able to select a new product to file your taxes, and you'll have to re-import and re-enter all of your info. The page states plainly that clearing your data can't be undone. Treat this as a real point of no return, not a soft reset. If any of your entered info was hard to reconstruct, imported W-2s, prior-year carryovers, confirm you can get those again before confirming.

image.caption: TurboTax's confirmation screen before clearing tax data, listing exactly what you lose and warning that the action can't be undone.

steps.heading: Choose No, thanks or clear your data
steps.body: Two buttons sit side by side: "No, thanks" backs you out with nothing changed, and "I want to clear my tax data" commits to the wipe. If you're not fully certain, back out and review your Federal and State sections first. What feels like a reason to start over is sometimes a smaller fix within a single section, which costs far less than redoing entries you'd already finished.

steps.heading: What to do once Clear & Start Over is no longer available
steps.body: TurboTax's own instructions are specific about what closes this door: submitting payment, having the TurboTax fee deducted from your refund, or registering your product each independently disable Clear & Start Over, whether or not the return has technically been filed with the IRS yet. Once you're past that point, the correct path is an amended return, typically Form 1040-X for individuals, filed separately. It is not a cancellation of the original. Starting a new account doesn't undo an already-filed return either; TurboTax allows up to five accounts per email, but a fresh account only gives you a fresh return, not a way to erase what the IRS already has on file.

troubleshooting.problem: Clear & Start Over doesn't appear, or the option is grayed out
troubleshooting.cause: TurboTax disables it once you've submitted payment, had the fee deducted from your refund, or registered your product, even if you haven't formally filed yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Check whether any of those three things has happened. If one has, edit the return manually instead of trying to restart it.

troubleshooting.problem: The return is already filed and contains an error
troubleshooting.cause: TurboTax blocks clearing tax data entirely after filing, since the return is already on record with the IRS.
troubleshooting.fix: File an amended return, Form 1040-X for individuals, instead of attempting to restart the original.

troubleshooting.problem: Considering a second TurboTax account to avoid clearing the first
troubleshooting.cause: Up to five accounts can share one email, which some people use to start a fresh return without touching the original.
troubleshooting.fix: Understand this creates a separate return; it doesn't cancel or delete a return that's already been filed under the first account.

faq.question: Does TurboTax have a literal cancel return button?
faq.answer: No. The closest equivalent is Clear & Start Over, found under Tax Tools in the sidebar, which erases your entered data so you can begin again, but only before payment, registration, or fee deduction has happened.

faq.question: Can I cancel a TurboTax return after it's already been filed?
faq.answer: No. TurboTax blocks clearing tax data once a return has been filed. You'd need to file an amended return instead.

faq.question: What exactly disables Clear & Start Over?
faq.answer: Three things, according to TurboTax's own instructions: submitting payment, having the TurboTax fee deducted from your refund, or registering your product. Any one of them closes the option, independent of whether you've formally filed.

faq.question: Do I have to re-enter everything if I clear my return?
faq.answer: Yes. TurboTax states upfront that you'll need to re-import and re-enter all of your info after clearing, and you'll also be able to pick a different product to file with.

faq.question: Is there a faster fix than clearing the whole return?
faq.answer: Often. Check the Federal or State section causing the issue first. Many problems that feel like they need a full restart are fixable within a single section.

references.label: TurboTax Support: How do I clear and start over in TurboTax Online?

verifiedNote: Sign-in, Tax home, and confirmation screens come from a recorded TurboTax Online walkthrough. The menu path and the exact conditions that disable Clear & Start Over were checked against TurboTax's own support article in September 2026 and corrected: the option sits inside a Tools submenu under Tax Tools, not next to it, and it's disabled by three specific actions (payment, fee deduction, or registration), not simply by having "already filed," which is how the previous draft summarized it.
